q-132483.name: Question 1
q-132483.problem: On a webpage, visitors arrive continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one every $15$ seconds.  Determine the probability of waiting for the next visitor for less than $0.5$ minutes.  Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
q-132483.worked_solution:
Since visitors arrive continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next visitor appears using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time between two consecutive visitor arrivals. Since visitors arrive on average every $15$ seconds, the rate is $\lambda =60÷15=4$ visitors per minute.

The time between two consecutive visitor arrivals can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =4,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(4).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}4{e}^{-4x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of waiting for the next visitor for less than 
$0.5$ minutes is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<0.5) & ={\int }_{0}^{0.5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{0.5}4{e}^{-4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}{|}_{0}^{0.5} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.8647\end{aligned}
$$

q-132486.name: Question 2
q-132486.problem: A monitor issues a warning signal when an action is needed as part of a production process. Signals occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one every $0.2$ minutes.  Determine the probability of the next signal occurring within the next $0.4$ minutes. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
q-132486.worked_solution:
Since the monitor issues a warning signal continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next signal appears using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time between successive signals. Since the monitor issues a warning signal every $0.2=\frac{1}{5}$ minutes, the rate is $\lambda =5$ signals per minute.

The times between two successive signals can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda =5,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(5).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-5x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of the next signal occurring within the next $0.4$ minutes is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<0.4) & ={\int }_{0}^{0.4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{0.4}5{e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-5x}|}_{0}^{0.4} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{0} \\  & =1-{e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.8647\end{aligned}
$$

q-132558.name: Question 3
q-132558.problem: The waiting time for one customer to be served at a cafeteria varies continuously, independently, and at a constant average rate of one person served every $4$  minutes. Determine the probability that the next person is served at least $2$ minutes after the previous one. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
q-132558.worked_solution:
Since the waiting time for one customer to be served at the cafeteria varies continuously, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until serving the next person as an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time needed to serve the next person. The time needed to serve the next person can be modeled as an exponential random variable. Since one person is served every $4$ minutes on average, the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{4},$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{4}).
$$

 In this case, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-x/4}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the next person will be served at least $2$ minutes after the previous one is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-x/4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/4}{|}_{2}^{\infty } \\  & =-{e}^{-\infty }+{e}^{-2/4} \\  & =0+{e}^{-1/2} \\  & ={e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.6065.\end{aligned}
$$

q-254581.name: Question 4
q-254581.problem:
A customer support team resolves tickets continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of $1$ ticket every $5$ minutes. If a ticket has been open for $20$ minutes already, what is the probability that it will remain unresolved for at least another $10$ minutes? Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

The required probability is
{{field-1}}.
q-254581.worked_solution:
Since the customer support team resolves tickets continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next ticket is resolved using an exponential distribution.

Let $X$ be the ticket resolving time, in minutes. Since the team resolves $1$ ticket every $5$ minutes on average, the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{5}$ tickets per minute, and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{5}).
$$

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. So, given two positive real numbers $s,t,$ we have that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{1}{5},$ $s=20,$ and $t=10.$ 

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>20+10\,|\,X>20) & =P(X>10) \\  & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(1/5)\cdot (10)} \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.135.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Since the customer support team resolves tickets continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next ticket is resolved using an exponential distribution.

Let X be the ticket resolving time, in minutes. Since the team resolves 1 ticket every 5 minutes on average, the rate is λ=15 tickets per minute, and we can write

X∼Exp(15).

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. So, given two positive real numbers s,t, we have that P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t)=e−λt.

In our case, we have λ=15, s=20, and t=10.

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get P(X>20+10|X>20)=P(X>10)=e−λt=e−(1/5)⋅(10)=e−2≈0.135.

q-254609.name: Question 5
q-254609.problem:
While riding on a road, a cyclist encounters potholes continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of $4$ potholes per hour. If the cyclist has not encountered any potholes in the past $30$ minutes, what is the probability that he will encounter a pothole in the next $10$ minutes? Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

The required probability is
{{field-1}}.
q-254609.worked_solution:
Since the cyclist encounters potholes continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next pothole as an exponential distribution.

Let $X$ be the time, in minutes, until the cyclist encounters the next pothole. Since the cyclist encounters, on average, $4$ potholes per hour (or $1$ pothole every $15$ minutes), the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{15}$ potholes per minute, and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{15}).
$$

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. Therefore, given two positive real numbers $s,t,$ we have that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{1}{15},$ $s=30,$ and $t=10.$ 

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 30+10\,|\,X>30) & =P(X\le 10) \\  & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(1/15)\cdot (10)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-2/3} \\  & ≈0.487.\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 0.487

Let X be the time, in minutes, until the cyclist encounters the next pothole. Since the cyclist encounters, on average, 4 potholes per hour (or 1 pothole every 15 minutes), the rate is λ=115 potholes per minute, and we can write X∼Exp(115).

Recall that exponential random variables have the memoryless property. Therefore, given two positive real numbers s,t, we have that P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t)=e−λt.

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows: P(X≤s+t|X>s)=1−P(X>s+t|X>s)=1−e−λt

In our case, we have λ=115, s=30, and t=10.

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get P(X≤30+10|X>30)=P(X≤10)=1−e−λt=1−e−(1/15)⋅(10)=1−e−2/3≈0.487.
